name: Anger
oracle_text:
Haste
As long as this card is in your graveyard and you control a Mountain, creatures you control have haste.
blocked_sentences: As long as this card is in your graveyard and you control a Mountain, creatures you control have haste.

needs.what: a static ability that applies while its source card sits in a graveyard -- the static-ability walk must gather statics from graveyard cards as well as battlefield permanents, and the ability must be able to declare that graveyard is where it is active
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `active_zones` exists on the ability schema and accepts "graveyard", but the loader only reads it on the activated and triggered branches; `_compile_static` builds its Ability without it, so every static is pinned to the battlefield default. The pipeline agrees: `_battlefield_statics` is documented as 'every active static ability on the battlefield' and is the only source of statics, so a static written on Anger would switch on the moment Anger resolved as a 2/2 -- granting the team haste from play, which the card never does -- and switch off the moment it died, which is exactly when the card is supposed to work.

needs.what: a static `condition` predicate that asks which zone the static's own source is in, so "as long as this card is in your graveyard" can gate the grant rather than being implied by where the card happens to be
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `zone_is` is in `condition_keys` and in the cost-reduction condition heads, but `static_condition_keys` is a separate, smaller language (all, any, cmp, counters, exists, has_city_s_blessing, is_attached, is_your_turn, not, top_of_library) and carries no zone predicate at all. `exists` can only ask about other objects via a selector, not about the source's own zone, so the graveyard half of the condition cannot be written even if the engine gathered the static.
